newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber quiet, market looks for leads.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber quiet, market looks for leads.

text.p: Trading in the Singapore rubber market was quiet by midsession on Friday with players waiting for leads and trying to assess the impact of Thailand's decision to default on a rubber deal, traders said.
"Everybody is basically waiting for leads and nothing was done this morning. People are still trying to gauge what the impact of the Thai decision will be," a dealer said.
Thai Deputy Prime Minister Sukhawich Rangsitphol said on Thursday Bangkok will not take delivery of 23,100 tonnes of rubber to trim losses on an official scheme to shore up local rubber prices.
The market also wanted to see if Michelin, which most in the trade believe has not finished their monthly buying programme, will resume buying later in the day.
"We have not seen any of the major consumers ask for offers. We're hoping that will change this afternoon," a dealer said.
Weak regional currencies may prompt some, however, to stay out to see if the situation will calm down, one dealer said.
At 0445 GMT, September RSS3 was indicated steady at 94.00 U.S. cents a kg. September RSS1 was indicated at 138.00-140.00 Singapore cents (93-95 U.S. cents) a kg from 138.00 cents.
